roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is a dominant force in VGC due to its Drought ability, which provides sun support that enhances its own Fire-type attacks while enabling a strong offensive and defensive playstyle for the team. Its massive Special Attack stat and solid Speed allow it to function as a powerful sweeper, and its typing provides useful resistances and coverage options. Starting with a high-impact Mega ensures a strong foundation for the rest of the draft.

roster.name: Torkoal
roster.rationale: Torkoal provides a secondary Drought setter, ensuring sun remains active even if Mega Charizard Y is KOed or unable to Mega Evolve. It also offers a bulky Fire-type presence with strong defensive stats and access to utility moves like Yawn and Stealth Rock, addressing the need for a defensive backbone. Its low Speed can be mitigated by sun-boosted attacks and support from Tailwind or Trick Room later.

roster.name: Volcarona
roster.rationale: Volcarona is a premier sun abuser with Chlorophyll or Quiver Dance, synergizing perfectly with Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal's Drought. It provides a strong Fire-type offensive presence and covers Grass- and Steel-types that threaten the core. Its Bug typing also offers useful resistances to Fighting and Ground, while its Quiver Dance set can sweep under sun or even without it. This pick fills the role of a high-speed offensive threat while maintaining flexibility.

roster.name: Alolan Ninetales
roster.rationale: Alolan Ninetales (14) fills the Dragon/Ground answer role with its Fairy typing and Snow Warning, providing speed control via hail and disrupting opposing weather. It also offers a secondary Ice/Fairy offensive presence to threaten Grass- and Dragon-types, complementing the sun core while adding flexibility to matchups.

roster.name: Toxapex
roster.rationale: Toxapex provides a Fire-resistant, bulky Water-type that walls physical attackers and disrupts opponents with Baneful Bunker, Toxic Spikes, and Scald. Its Regenerator ability ensures longevity, and it covers Volcarona’s Rock weakness while patching my team’s vulnerability to Water and Fighting types.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult provides critical speed control, Tailwind, and a fast, versatile offensive presence with Dragon/Dark/Ghost coverage. It outspeeds and pressures common threats like Garchomp, Volcarona, and opposing Dragapult, while its ability to run U-turn or status moves adds pivot utility. At 14 points, it fits budget constraints while addressing speed and offensive synergy needs.

roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Shadow Tag is the most game-warping ability in VGC — trapping eliminates the opponent's ability to pivot, and 170 SpA / 130 Spe makes Mega Gengar an elite special nuke that can pick off trapped targets. At 18 points I keep 82 for nine more picks, which is plenty to build speed control, Intimidate support, and a physical complement around the trap-and-kill gameplan. The name encodes GLM (my identity), Ghost (Gengar's type), and Labyrinth (Shadow Tag — you can't escape).

roster.name: Maushold
roster.rationale: Maushold is the premier redirection support in the format — Friend Guard reduces all damage to adjacent allies by 25%, and Follow Me pulls attacks away from Mega Gengar so it can safely trap and eliminate targets. With two weather coaches (Drought/Drizzle) still holding 80+ points and likely seeking redirection for their sweepers, Maushold may not survive to my next pick at 19. Technician-boosted Population Bomb also gives it real offensive output, making it more than just a passive support mon.

roster.name: Klefki
roster.rationale: Klefki is the top speed-control target from my board — Prankster Tailwind, Reflect, Light Screen, and Thunder Wave support perfectly complements Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping and Maushold's Follow Me/Friend Guard utility. Steel/Fairy typing adds valuable defensive coverage against the Dragon, Dark, and Fairy attackers opponents have already drafted. At 11 points it leaves 55 for 7 picks, keeping my budget flexible for Intimidate, a wallbreaker, and defensive backbone.

roster.name: Gyarados
roster.rationale: Arcanine is gone, so Gyarados becomes my top Intimidate option — it doubles as a Water-type answer to the Droughtfire Dynasts' fire core and can run Dragon Dance as an offensive mode or a bulky Intimidate pivot. At 11 points it preserves budget flexibility better than Aegislash (14) while filling two needs at once (Intimidate + weather counterplay).

roster.name: Aegislash
roster.rationale: Aegislash is the premier defensive backbone still on the board and the most at-risk pick for my needs — Steel/Ghost with Stance Change gives me a versatile shield/blade that checks Fairy, Dragon, and Normal threats while outputting strong damage. It pairs excellently with Gyarados's Intimidate and Klefki's Steel/Fairy typing to form a solid defensive core, and at 14 points it leaves me 30 for 5 remaining picks, fitting my budget plan of ~6/pick average.

roster.name: Rotom-Heat
roster.rationale: Rotom-Heat's Levitate gives a second Ground immunity alongside Gyarados, protecting the Ground-weak Klefki and Aegislash from Garchomp and Earthquake spam, while its Electric/Fire typing resists Fire to shore up the sun matchup and provides Electric STAB to punish rain teams like Pelipper+Basculegion. At 12 points it leaves 18 for four remaining picks, enough to grab a cheap physical wallbreaker (Machamp 4) and fill out utility and weather counterplay.

roster.name: Machamp
roster.rationale: Machamp at 4 points is the best-value physical wallbreaker on the board — No Guard guarantees Dynamic Punch lands with 100% confusion, and 130 base Atk with coverage like Knock Off, Ice Punch, and Fire Punch breaks through the Steel-types and fat mons my special-heavy roster struggles with. This keeps my budget plan intact at 4+5+5+4=18, preserving flexibility for Vaporeon, Serperior, and a utility pick in the final three rounds.

roster.name: Vaporeon
roster.rationale: Vaporeon (5) is the rain counterplay I flagged as critical — Water Absorb hard-stops Pelipper/Basculegion-Male from Drizzle Dominators, and it adds a bulky Water-type with reliable recovery that my roster currently lacks. At 5 points it keeps my budget flexible for two more picks (9 left, need 5+4 or similar). Serperior (5) remains the top priority for next pick.

roster.name: Serperior
roster.rationale: Serperior is the top priority from my previous note and is still available at 5 points. Contrary Leaf Storm gives me a Grass-type win condition I completely lack, covering the Water/Ground types that trouble my current roster, while its 113 Speed outspeeds key threats like Garchomp, Volcarona, and base Gyarados. This leaves exactly 4 points for my final pick, where Ditto is the ideal revenge-killer against weather sweepers and Mega evolutions.

roster.name: Ditto
roster.rationale: Ditto at exactly 4 points is the perfect final pick, providing revenge-killing against the many weather and Mega sweeper threats across the league (Mega Charizard Y sun, Pelipper+Basculegion rain, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Metagross, Sneasler). With Choice Scarf Imposter Ditto, I gain a catch-all speed-control answer that punishes setup and stat-boosted sweepers, filling the one gap my roster lacked. No other 4-point option addresses this need as cleanly.

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the single most role-compressed support in VGC: Intimidate cycling via Parting Shot, Fake Out pressure, and pivoting Fire/Dark coverage lets me anchor any archetype I draft next without locking into one mode. The other 18-point slot I'm watching (Farigiraf) is more specialized, and the 19s are restricted-style pieces I can wait a round on — Intimidate cycling is uniquely irreplaceable. At 18 with 82 left across 9 picks I'm on a 9.1-point average, which lets me still grab a 16-19 centerpiece plus a flexible mid-tier bench.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo gives Incineroar a premium special spread attacker and the Steel defensive profile our roster lacks; Incineroar reciprocally resists its Fire, Ghost, and Dark weaknesses while creating safe Make It Rain turns with Fake Out and Parting Shot. Its typing plus Good as Gold is excellent into the drafted Sneasler-Whimsicott core, and Ghost typing preserves switching options against Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag. At 16 points, it leaves enough room to pursue Mega Aerodactyl as the fast, Ground-immune Tailwind piece that patches the core's main weakness.

roster.name: Mega Aerodactyl
roster.rationale: Mega Aerodactyl at 17 fits the 18-point ceiling, gives me the Tailwind speed control pivot I need, Rock pressure into the Charizard Y / Torkoal sun team, and Ground immunity for my Incineroar pivot game. 130 base Speed with Tailwind outpaces every non-Mega on the board and lets me lead aggressively. This also pairs cleanly with Gholdengo's Make It Rain to delete Talonflame and other Flying types that would otherwise revenge me.

roster.name: Rotom-Mow
roster.rationale: Rotom-Mow adds a crucial Ground immunity and strong Grass/Electric pressure into rain, Rotom-Wash, Milotic, Primarina, and the Archaludon/Garchomp core. Its Volt Switch forms an excellent pivot cycle with Incineroar, while Mega Aerodactyl’s Tailwind helps it apply offensive pressure and Gholdengo benefits from Rotom drawing Grass-resistant targets.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: At 9 points Hatterene solves my biggest structural gaps without eating into the budget I need for five more picks. Magic Bounce neutralises the Prankster leads opposing Whimsicott / Klefki / Grimmsnarl will bring, Trick Room gives me an alternative gameplan against the slow, bulky cores (Floette/Kingambit, Mega Metagross/Sinistcha, Archaludon/Garchomp, Mega Blastoise/Sneasler) that outlast my fast Aerodactyl mode, and 136 SpA + 103 SpD with Fairy typing slots in as the bulky backbone I currently lack behind Incineroar. It also lets me pair Trick Room with Incineroar's Intimidate pivot in mirror-style matchups.

roster.name: Weavile
roster.rationale: Weavile is the fast physical attacker I'm missing to complement my special wallbreakers (Gholdengo, Rotom-Mow) and bulky backbone. 125 base speed pairs naturally with Mega Aerodactyl's Tailwind lead, plus Triple Axel hits the Engineers' Archaludon/Garchomp (and Mamoswine, Dragonite, Volcarona elsewhere) super effectively while Knock Off strips items from key targets like Mega Gengar, Maushold, Leftovers users, and Heavy-Duty Boots holders. At 9 points it leaves 21 for 4 more picks with the 13-point reserve intact, letting me round out with cheap Water/Ground/Disguise pieces later.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Gliscor is the best cheap structural patch: Ground/Flying gives the roster a valuable Ground immunity, an Electric immunity, and a strong answer to the Ground-heavy opposing board while Poison Heal supports durable pivoting. It also complements Incineroar and Rotom-Mow without competing for the Mega slot, and its Ground pressure helps punish the Steel- and Fire-heavy field. At only 3 points, it preserves flexibility for the final three picks.

roster.name: Araquanid
roster.rationale: Araquanid is the best use of this slot: Water Bubble gives the roster a powerful bulky Water attacker that functions naturally under Hatterene's Trick Room, while its Fire resistance and excellent special bulk improve the sun, rain, Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar matchups. It also leaves 7 points for the final two selections, allowing two meaningful low-cost utility picks instead of forcing 1-point fillers.

roster.name: Alcremie
roster.rationale: Alcremie adds valuable Fairy coverage into the league's Dragons and Dark-types while giving the roster a dedicated support option through Decorate, Helping Hand, and Sweet Veil or Aroma Veil. At base 64 Speed it also functions naturally in Hatterene's Trick Room mode, and its strong special bulk helps stabilize matchups where our current defensive core is pressured.

roster.rationale: Qwilfish adds a second Intimidate option while providing valuable disruption through Taunt and Haze, helping against setup and opposing Trick Room modes. Its Water/Poison typing gives the roster another Fairy check and a flexible Rain Dance option for disrupting the many sun teams in the league. The one unspent point is acceptable because Qwilfish offers more practical utility than the available one-point fillers.

draftRoster.rationale: Sinistcha (18) is the premier redirection piece still on the board: Rage Powder protects Mega Metagross from Ghost and Dark moves while it sets up or attacks. It thrives in Farigiraf's Trick Room with base 70 Speed, provides a crucial Ground resist for Metagross, and Hospitality offers passive sustain every switch-in. Heatproof also blunts the Sun and Fire-type threats from Droughtfire Dynasts and Smoldering Intimidates.

draftRoster.name: Noivern
draftRoster.rationale: Noivern (9 pts) compresses two urgent needs into one slot: a Ground immunity (Flying-type) and a fast Tailwind setter (123 base Speed) to enable Mega Metagross's fast mode. Telepathy also synergises with potential spread moves from Primarina. At 9 points it leaves a comfortable 23 for the final 5 picks, keeping the path open for Fake Out and a secondary physical attacker.

draftRoster.name: Conkeldurr
draftRoster.rationale: Conkeldurr (7) is a perfect TR abuser alongside Farigiraf: 140 base Attack, 45 Speed, and Guts for status immunity. It directly answers Kingambit with Fighting STAB, resists Dark (shoring up a stacked weakness across Metagross, Farigiraf, and Sinistcha), and brings Mach Punch priority. At 7 points it leaves 16 for the final 4 picks — excellent value that keeps the budget flexible.

draftRoster.name: Hisuian Goodra
draftRoster.rationale: Hisuian Goodra (6) patches the glaring special-bulk gap with 150 SpD and adds a Steel/Dragon that thrives in TR (60 Spe). Sap Sipper provides a Grass immunity, shutting down Spore and protecting Primarina/Sinistcha. At 6 points it leaves 10 for the final three picks—enough room for Fake Out and a pivot.

draftRoster.name: Toxicroak
draftRoster.rationale: Fake Out is the single biggest gap on this roster, and Toxicroak at 4 points is the best value remaining Fake Out user. Dry Skin provides a Water immunity that helps against rain matchups, Sucker Punch adds priority, and its middling 85 Speed works in both TR and mid-speed modes. The 4x Psychic weakness is manageable with two Steel-types and Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocking priority. Leaves 6 points for 2 picks — ideally Overqwil (4) for Intimidate next.

draftRoster.name: Overqwil
draftRoster.rationale: Overqwil (4 pts) is the best available Intimidate user and my top target per the draft plan. Dark/Poison typing adds a Psychic immunity and valuable resistances (Grass, Ghost, Dark, Poison) without compounding my Ice weakness. Swift Swim also gives me a situational anti-rain tool. Leaves 2 pts for a final Ground-immune pivot like Rotom.

draftRoster.name: Tauros
draftRoster.rationale: Rotom is gone, so Tauros (2 pts) is the best pivot left: Intimidate stacks with Overqwil to neuter physical threats, 110 Speed makes it a genuine fast-mode attacker under Noivern's Tailwind, and Sheer Force + Life Orb gives it real offensive bite with Body Slam/Rock Slide coverage. Its Normal typing also provides a Ghost immunity that protects Farigiraf from opposing Ghost spam, rounding out the defensive synergy.

teambuilds.rationale: The opponent brings sun or snow heavy offense with Charizard-Mega-Y, Torkoal, Volcarona, Alolan Ninetales, Dragapult, and other threats. We counter weather domination with Hippowdon's Sand Stream to overwrite Drought/Snow, while Mega Blastoise pressures Fire-types and deals massive water damage. Sneasler and Whimsicott control the pace with Fake Out/Tailwind, and Clefable and Rotom round out defensive utility and pivoting.

We counter the opponent's rain and weather options (Pelipper, Basculegion, Ninetales) by bringing Hippowdon to set Sand Stream, alongside Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind speed control. Mega Blastoise provides incredible special offense with Mega Launcher, Sneasler and Kleavor offer high-pressure physical offense, and Clefable acts as a bulky Unaware redirection pivot.

Rain core (Pelipper + Basculegion) punishes Talonflame/Mamoswine while boosting Water STAB; double Prankster (Grimmsnarl/Sableye) handles Mega Lopunny speed and Kingambit with priority/Taunt/Parting Shot; Garganacl walls physical threats and Hisuian Arcanine pivots with Intimidate. This spread covers opponent's Fairy/Steel/Dark cores and speed demons.

Rain core (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion) punishes their fast physical threats (Sneasler, Kleavor, Scolipede) while overriding potential sand; double Prankster (Grimmsnarl/Sableye) handles Whimsicott and provides speed control/Taunt; Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivots into Mega Blastoise/Zoroark; Garganacl walls physical attackers and sets Stealth Rock. Item spread avoids overlap and enables rain sweep + utility.

Mega Lopunny is the primary fast-mode attacker, using Fake Out and Scrappy-boosted Fighting pressure while Talonflame supplies priority Tailwind and disruption. Milotic punishes Incineroar or Qwilfish Intimidate with Competitive and provides Icy Wind plus bulky Water pressure; Mamoswine threatens Mega Aerodactyl, Gliscor, Rotom-Mow, and Gholdengo. Kingambit is the late-game Dark/Steel cleaner and further punishes Intimidate with Defiant, while Scrafty gives a second Fake Out, Intimidate, Snarl, and Knock Off mode against special attackers.

The opponent's team is built around physical attackers (Sneasler, Kleavor, Mega Blastoise, Scolipede) and fast threats (Whimsicott, Sneasler, Hisuian Zoroark). To counter this, we leverage Drought from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal to empower sun-based sweepers like Volcarona and Mega Victreebel. Toxapex provides a Fire-resistant bulky Water to absorb hits and disrupt setup sweepers, while Dragapult offers speed control and offensive pressure. Arbok's Intimidate softens physical attackers, and Mega Beedrill provides Adaptability-boosted STAB priority to pick off weakened foes.

Mega Floette is the primary win condition, using Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin to punish Grimmsnarl, Sableye, Absol, and the Fire/Rock threats while Energy Ball pressures the rain core. Milotic and Dedenne provide redundant answers to Pelipper and Basculegion with Competitive, Icy Wind, Nuzzle, and Electric attacks; Talonflame supplies Tailwind, Taunt, and weather disruption. Scrafty gives Fake Out, Intimidate, Snarl, and Knock Off utility, while Mamoswine pressures Hisuian Arcanine, Ninetales, Emolga, and Mawile with Ground- and Ice-type attacks.

Target Mega Metagross and Hisuian Goodra as the primary threats. Mega Charizard Y provides Drought to enable sun-boosted Fire moves and Solar Beam, pressuring Metagross and Goodra. Volcarona sweeps late-game with Quiver Dance under sun, while Dragapult provides speed control with **Dragon Dance** and offensive pressure. Toxapex walls Primarina and Sinistcha with **Muddy Water** and Toxic Spikes, Arbok Intimidates physical attackers like Metagross, and Torkoal backs up Drought while disrupting with Yawn and Body Press.

Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag is the central threat; Tinkaton's Fairy/Steel typing lets it switch in safely on either STAB and chip with Knock Off, while Archaludon's Life Orb Dark Pulse threatens an OHKO. Garchomp and Arcanine provide Ground and Fire coverage to handle the Steel/Ghost core of Aegislash and Klefki, plus Intimidate support to blunt physical attackers like Machamp and Gyarados. Rotom-Wash on Choice Scarf outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame to pivot with Volt Switch and spread burns, and Blaziken cleans up late with Speed Boost after Focus Sash guarantees it survives turn one.

Mega Metagross is the central threat; Arcanine's Flare Blitz and Garchomp's Earthquake handle it while Intimidate softens physical hits. Starmie outspeeds Noivern and OHKOes with Ice Beam. Blaziken Speed Boosts past Goodra-Hisui and Conkeldurr with Close Combat. Tinkaton provides Fake Out redirection and Play Rough for Dark/Fighting types. Rotom-Wash burns physical attackers and pivots with Volt Switch.

We bring Mega Blastoise, Sneasler, Whimsicott, and Hippowdon as our core four (backed by Clefable and Rotom) to handle Mega Lopunny, Mega Floette, Kingambit, and Mamoswine. Hippowdon sets up Sand and handles physical threats, Whimsicott gives Prankster Tailwind support, and Mega Blastoise plus Sneasler break through their defensive backbone with powerful STAB and coverage, respecting the strict 32 Champions EV cap per stat.

Mega Gengar at 200 Speed ties Jolteon and outspeeds the rest of the opponent's roster; Shadow Ball OHKOs Starmie, Dazzling Gleam chunks Garchomp, and Focus Blast can OHKO Archaludon. Klefki provides Prankster screens and Thunder Wave to slow Jolteon/Starmie/Garchomp. Gyarados Intimidate weakens physical attackers (Garchomp, Blaziken, Arcanine) and Dragon Dance sweeps at +1 (219 Spe outspeeds everything). Aegislash resists Dragon/Fighting and checks Garchomp/Blaziken with Close Combat for Archaludon/Tinkaton and Wide Guard for spread protection. Rotom-Heat burns physical attackers and Overheats Tinkaton/Roserade. Ditto Scarf revenge-kills Speed Boost Blaziken or any boosted threat.

Trick Room mode: Farigiraf sets TR under Armor Tail + Mental Herb, then four slow breakers (Primarina, Sinistcha, Hisuian Goodra, Conkeldurr) sweep under TR while Mega Metagross cleans up with Tough Claws-boosted coverage. Opponent's fast threats (Garchomp, Arcanine, Jolteon, Starmie) are flipped by TR; Ice Punch, Moonblast, and Draco Meteor handle Garchomp; EQ and Fire Blast answer Archaludon/Tinkaton; Matcha Gotcha destroys Rotom-Wash.

This opponent’s team is heavy on Steel, Dragon, and Water types (Archaludon, Garchomp, Rotom-Wash, Tinkaton, Starmie), which threaten our core with their bulk and offensive pressure. We prioritize **Drought** to weaken Water and boost Fire-type attacks, **Chlorophyll** to outspeed and pressure with Grass/Poison coverage, and **disruption** to handle their defensive synergy. Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona will serve as primary sweepers under sun, while Toxapex and Arbok provide Intimidate and defensive utility. Mega Victreebel adds Chlorophyll-boosted Grass coverage to threaten Rotom-Wash and Garchomp, and Arbok provides Intimidate support and disruptive utility with Glare and Sucker Punch.

Talonflame provides immediate Tailwind and Taunt pressure against Whimsicott, Sneasler, and setup options, while Mega Floette threatens broad Fairy damage into Sneasler and the opposing roster. Milotic checks Mega Blastoise with Competitive, special bulk, and Icy Wind; Mamoswine pressures Kleavor, Hippowdon, Rotom, and Zoroark-Hisui while benefiting from either Tailwind or Musharna's Trick Room. Scrafty supplies Fake Out, Intimidate, Snarl, and Dark coverage, with Musharna enabling a slower mode and Telepathy support for Mamoswine's spread attacks.

Dual-mode team against a roster built around Mega Floette/Lopunny, Talonflame, and Kingambit. Fast mode: Mega Aerodactyl + Weavile lead with Rock Slide spread and priority Ice Shard to handle Lopunny (135 Spe), Talonflame (Gale Wings), and Floette. Trick Room mode: Hatterene sets TR for Araquanid, whose Water Bubble + Mystic Water boosted Liquidation deletes Mamoswine/Milotic/Kingambit. Incineroar provides Intimidate pivots and Fake Out, while Gholdengo's Good as Gold + Steel/Ghost coverage walls Floette, Milotic, and Musharna special attackers.

Opponent brings sun through Charizard Y + Torkoal with Volcarona abusing it, plus fast threats Dragapult and Beedrill, and bulky Toxapex. My plan is Trick Room to flip their speed: lead Farigiraf + Sinistcha, where Armor Tail blocks any priority and Heatproof Sinistcha uses Rage Powder to redirect Fire moves away while Farigiraf sets TR. Mega Metagross cleans with Rock Slide for their 4x Fire/Bug weaknesses and Tough Claws Zen Headbutt for Toxapex. Conkeldurr provides Wide Guard against spread Heat Wave/Eruption/Blizzard and hits hard under TR. Primarina OHKOs Dragapult with Moonblast and pressures Toxapex with Psychic Noise. Overqwil cycles Intimidate to neuter physical Dragapult/Beedrill and threatens with Crunch.

Opponent's fastest threats are Mega Aerodactyl (150 Spe) and Weavile (125 Spe); Mega Gengar hits 200 Spe after Mega Evolution to outspeed both, traps with Shadow Tag, and nukes Gholdengo/Hatterene with Shadow Ball. Klefki provides Prankster screens and Thunder Wave to paralyze Aero/Weavile, while Gyarados adds Intimidate and Dragon Dance for physical pressure with Waterfall hitting Aero SE. Aegislash is the defensive Steel/Ghost pivot with Wide Guard to block Rock Slide and Earthquake, Rotom-Heat Overheat OHKOs Gholdengo and burns physical attackers, and Ditto with Choice Scarf revenge-kills any fast threat or setup sweeper.

Opponent runs double Drought (Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal) sun with fast Fire/Bug threats (Volcarona, Mega Beedrill) and Dragapult. Rock Slide from Garchomp and Archaludon 4x OHKOes Charizard Y, Volcarona, Toucannon, and Mega Beedrill. Starmie outspeeds the sun core and Ice Beams Dragapult. Blaziken Speed Boosts behind sun-boosted Flare Blitz to clean. Rotom-Wash burns physical attackers and Tinkaton provides Fairy coverage for Dragapult plus redirection.

Opponent has heavy physical attackers (Mega Metagross, Conkeldurr, Tauros, Overqwil) and bulky special walls (Primarina, Hisuian Goodra). I bring Incineroar for Intimidate + Fake Out pivoting, Gholdengo to immune Fighting/Normal and threaten Sinistcha/Farigiraf with Ghost, Mega Aerodactyl for speed control and Rock Slide spread that crushes Noivern/Metagross, Weavile as a fast Knock Off + Ice Shard lead that pressures Goodra and Noivern, Hatterene for Magic Bounce vs Sinistcha and Trick Room reversal, and Gliscor as a Ground-immune Poison Heal pivot that handles Overqwil and Conkeldurr's Fighting coverage.

Fast-mode offense with Mega Aero outspeeding Mega Gengar (222 > 145) and Weavile (194) threatening Gengar with priority Fake Out and STAB Knock Off. Incineroar pivots with Intimidate + Parting Shot to weaken Machamp and Aegislash. Hatterene's Magic Bounce reflects Klefki's Spikes/Thunder Wave and sets Trick Room for the slow Hatterene/Rotom-Mow/Gholdengo core. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks status and Make It Rain shreds Maushold. Rotom-Mow's Levitate ignores Earthquake and hits Gyarados/Vaporeon with Thunderbolt/Leaf Storm.

TR mode with Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocking Incineroar's Fake Out to safely set Trick Room. Mega Metagross anchors with Tough Claws-boosted Iron Head to OHKO Hatterene and Hammer Arm to destroy Weavile. Primarina's Life Orb Hydro Pump OHKOs Incineroar and Mega Aerodactyl. Sinistcha brings Shadow Ball for Gholdengo and Rage Powder support. Hisuian Goodra walls Rotom-Mow and uses Fire Blast for Gholdengo coverage. Overqwil adds Intimidate to neuter physical threats plus Crunch for Gholdengo and Gunk Shot for Fairies.

Rain core (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion) punishes their Gyarados/Vaporeon while Basculegion's Wave Crash/Last Respects pressures the field; double Prankster (Grimmsnarl/Sableye) handles Klefki/Maushold/Ditto with Taunt/Parting Shot; Hisuian Arcanine provides Intimidate pivot and priority; Garganacl walls physical threats like Machamp/Aegislash. Sun mode is secondary but Ninetales is benched to keep item spread clean.

Opponent's rain core (Pelipper+Basculegion-Swift Swim) and dual Prankster support (Grimmsnarl/Sableye) demand speed control and Water immunity. Vaporeon's Water Absorb hard-counters rain Water moves while Klefki's Prankster TWave slows Swift Swim Basculegion below Mega Gengar's 200 Speed for a Shadow Ball KO. Rotom-Heat Thunderbolt OHKOs Pelipper and Overheat nukes Mawile. Machamp's No Guard Dynamic Punch provides guaranteed confusion hax and Close Combat breaks Garganacl. Aegislash's Wide Guard shields the team from Rock Slide and Earthquake spread damage while Flash Cannon hits Fairy types SE.

Mega Lopunny and Talonflame provide immediate pressure and Tailwind-based speed control, with Fake Out, priority Brave Bird, and Taunt disrupting the opponent’s sun offense. Milotic’s Rain Dance and Icy Wind answer Drought and support the slower attackers, while Thick Fat Mamoswine handles Fire-heavy compositions and threatens Charizard, Volcarona, and Toxapex. Scrafty supplies Intimidate, Snarl, and Fake Out against mixed offense, and Supreme Overlord Kingambit gives the team a durable late-game cleaner into Dragapult and the weakened Fire core.

Target Mega Floette and Kingambit as the primary threats. Lead with Torkoal + Arbok to set Sun and Intimidate, softening physical attackers. Mega Evolve Charizard Y to activate Drought and threaten Sun-boosted Fire moves. Toxapex disrupts with Toxic Spikes and handles Milotic with its bulk. Mega Victreebel sweeps under Sun with Chlorophyll, handling Grass-weak threats like Mamoswine and Altaria. Dragapult provides Tailwind support and speed control to outspeed fast threats like Talonflame and Mega Lopunny. Arbok and Toxapex handle Fairy-types with Poison coverage.

We bring Sneasler, Whimsicott, Mega Blastoise, and Hippowdon to handle the Ghostly Labyrinth Masters threat core. Whimsicott sets Tailwind and controls the board with Prankster Encore/Taunt against support like Klefki or Serperior, while Sneasler pressures with Fake Out disruption and STABs. Mega Blastoise provides incredible bulk and Mega Launcher-boosted special attacks (Aura Sphere, Water Pulse, Dark Pulse) to melt Aegislash, Rotom-Heat, and Mega Gengar. Hippowdon sets Sand Stream to passively chip down fragile targets like Maushold and Gengar while offering reliable Earthquake and Slack Off recovery.

Opponent's core revolves around Mega Aerodactyl (191 Spe) and Weavile (163 Spe) as fast physical threats, Gholdengo blocking status, and Incineroar providing Intimidate. Archaludon with Sturdy + Electro Shot (4x vs Rock/Flying) walls Mega Aerodactyl; Arcanine's Intimidate neuters the physical spam while Flare Blitz punishes Weavile/Gholdengo/Rotom-Mow; Blaziken Speed-Boosts past the entire tier after one Protect; Rotom-Wash and Garchomp provide Water/Ground coverage for Incineroar and Fire coverage for Gholdengo; Tinkaton's Mold Breaker Thunder Wave bypasses Good as Gold and Play Rough handles Dark types.

Opponent brings Jolteon, Starmie, Garchomp, Archaludon, Tinkaton, and likely Blaziken or Arcanine. I run a fast-mode offense led by Mega Aerodactyl (187 Spe, outspeeds Jolteon) with Tailwind support, plus Weavile for Ice-priority on Garchomp/Blaziken and Fake Out disruption. Incineroar provides Intimidate and pivoting; Gholdengo acts as a Ghost-resistant defensive pivot immune to status; Hatterene offers Magic Bounce (reflecting Thunder Wave) and an emergency Trick Room option; Rotom-Mow hits Garchomp/Archaludon/Arcanine/Blaziken hard with Leaf Storm and pivots with Volt Switch.

Mega Gengar outspeeds the entire opponent roster (200 Spe) and OHKOs Sneasler with Psychic, traps with Shadow Tag, and hits Clefable hard with Sludge Bomb. Aegislash is a full counter to Sneasler (immune to Fighting and Poison) and walls Kleavor. Gyarados Intimidate + Crunch handles Hisuian Zoroark and provides physical pressure vs Hippowdon. Serperior at 181 Spe outspeeds everything except Sneasler/Whimsicott and threatens Blastoise-Mega and Hippowdon with Leaf Storm while snowballing with Contrary. Klefki provides Prankster screens and Thunder Wave to neuter the fast Unburden sweepers. Maushold gives Friend Guard support, Follow Me redirection, and Tidy Up for hazard control.

Rain core (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion) punishes their Water/Fairy and slow physical threats while providing speed control. Grimmsnarl + Sableye double Prankster for Taunt/screens and Fake Out pressure on Mega Metagross and Conkeldurr. Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate pivots and threatens Steel types; Garganacl walls physical attackers and sets Stealth Rock. Item spread avoids overlap and covers the open team sheet.

The opponent’s team is heavy on physical attackers (Mega Aerodactyl, Weavile, Gliscor, Incineroar) and Intimidate support, which threatens our physical sweepers. Gholdengo and Rotom-Mow add special bulk and disruption, while Araquanid and Alcremie provide defensive utility. We prioritize **Drought** to enable our Fire-types (Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona) and **Chlorophyll** sweepers (Victreebel) to outspeed and pressure their offensive threats. Toxapex and Alolan Ninetales provide defensive synergy and disruption, while Dragapult offers speed control and offensive pressure. Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona will dismantle their physical attackers, while Toxapex walls their Water-types and Alolan Ninetales disrupts with Aurora Veil and Fairy coverage.

Opponent brings Drizzle rain with Pelipper+Basculegion, Grimmsnarl Prankster screens, and Hisuian Arcanine Intimidate. I counter with Trick Room mode: Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks all Prankster disruption and priority while setting TR safely. Toxicroak's Dry Skin walls Water spam and heals in rain, Overqwil provides Intimidate and Swift Swim as rain insurance. Mega Metagross and Conkeldurr are the primary TR breakers, with Sinistcha offering spread healing/burn pressure via Matcha Gotcha and Strength Sap longevity. All six function under TR while carrying tools to handle rain if TR is denied.

Sun offense with Mega Charizard Y, Torkoal, Volcarona, Dragapult, A-Ninetales, and Toxapex is the likely opponent shell. I bring Mega Aerodactyl as my own Mega to outspeed everything (222 Spe) and 4x Rock Slide Charizard Y and Volcarona, with Wide Guard to block Heat Wave. Incineroar provides Intimidate and Fake Out pivots, Weavile adds Ice Shard priority to threaten Dragapult and A-Ninetales, Gholdengo is status-immune and hits Dragapult hard with Shadow Ball, Hatterene's Magic Bounce reflects Torkoal Yawn / Volcarona Stun Spore / Toxapex Toxic, and Gliscor pivots with U-turn, stalls Toxapex with Toxic, and is immune to Beedrill's Poison STAB if it shows up.

Rain core (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion) punishes their Fire types (Blaziken/Arcanine) and supports water spam while Ninetales offers sun mode to blunt Rotom-Wash/Starmie. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens and priority, Garganacl walls Garchomp/Archaludon physically, and Hisuian Arcanine pivots with Intimidate. Item spread avoids overlap and targets their speed tier and common threats.

Lead Talonflame with Mega Lopunny or Mamoswine to exploit Gale Wings Tailwind and immediately pressure Mega Gengar, Maushold, Klefki, Aegislash, and Serperior. Milotic checks the Water core while Haze removes Contrary, Moxie, and Aegislash boosts; Kingambit supplies strong Dark pressure and punishes opposing Intimidate with Defiant. Scrafty gives Fake Out, Intimidate, Snarl, and Taunt support, with the six using distinct items and Mega Lopunny as the sole Mega evolution.

Rain is their core with Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion, but Archaludon turns their weather against them with free 130 BP Electro Shots. Rotom-Wash abuses rain with boosted Hydro Pump and burns physical attackers. Garchomp handles Rock/Steel/Fire types with Earthquake, Arcanine provides Intimidate support and Fire coverage for Mawile/Garganacl, Tinkaton removes items and handles Dark/Ghost types with Play Rough, and Blaziken cleans up with Speed Boost.

Opponent brings one Mega (Floette or Lopunny) plus 5 of Kingambit, Milotic, Talonflame, Mamoswine, Scrafty, Musharna, Altaria, Dedenne. Mega Gengar outspeeds and OHKOs Floette with Sludge Bomb while Shadow Tag traps; Aegislash walls Floette Moonblast (NVE), is immune to Lopunny Close Combat, and Wide Guards spread moves; Klefki provides Prankster screens + Thunder Wave to neuter Lopunny/Talonflame speed; Machamp No Guard Dynamic Punch OHKOs Kingambit and spreads confusion; Rotom-Heat at 138 Spe outspeeds Mamoswine/Milotic to Will-O-Wisp physical threats and Thunderbolts Talonflame; Ditto Scarf revenge-kills any boosted or fast sweeper (especially Lopunny-Mega).

We bring a strong balance of offensive pressure and defensive pivot capabilities to handle Metagross Examination's threats like Mega Metagross, Primarina, and Conkeldurr. Mega Blastoise anchors our special offense and water power, Hisuian Zoroark applies mind games with Illusion while threatening Ghost/Dark coverage, Sneasler outspeeds and pressures with Unburden/Poison-Fighting offense, Clefable provides crucial Fairy support and Unaware tanking with Moonlight, Hippowdon sets sand and tanks physical hits, and Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind and disruption.
